notes: On 20 October 2024, a Niger militia opened fire on a vehicle killing three people, including the driver, along the Bangi-Kotonkoro Road, coded to the closest populated area Kotonkoro (Mariga, Niger). The commuters were on the way to the market when they were attacked. The militia also abducted some farmers harvesting rice on the farm.

On 18 January 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with the Katsina militia in Dangeza, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina) and killed a militiaman. The troops recovered an AK 47 rifle mounted on a motorcycle with two magazines and one Baofeng HHR. 1 fatality reported.

On 7 November 2022, a Niger militia attacked farmers in Injita (Muya, Niger), Zagzaga, Chibiani and Lagbe [coded separately] and killed 5 farmers. Dozens of others were wounded and cattle belonging to farmers in Zagzaga and adjoining communities were rustled. 5 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 1.
On 21 October 2023, for the second day, members of Sankwala community protested in Sankwala (Obanliku, Cross River) accusing the hospital of negligence over the death of a woman during childbirth.

Around 2 December 2022 (as reported), the air component of Operation Whirl Punch targeted and destroyed hideouts of Kaduna militia led by Alhaji Isiaka with rockets in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). There are no further details.

On 8 March 2024, Nigerian troops attacked an IS/BH camp and killed three militiamen in Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). The Army destroyed their enclaves and recovered two AK-47 rifles and a suicide vest.

On 4 December 2023, NDLEA operatives were engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group that blocked the road in an attempt to prevent the operatives from gaining access into Opuje community (Owan West, Edo) where a warehouse containing marijuana was located. Three operatives were wounded including one who sustained head injuries in a clash that lasted for two hours, their operational vehicles were riddled with bullets. At least three suspects were arrested.
On 4 April 2022, Sokoto militiamen attacked a police checkpoint near Dogon Kare in Tureta LGA (Sokoto). One police personnel operation vehicle was set ablaze; casualties unknown.

On 11 April 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 8 passengers from commercial bus on the Emohua-Kalabari road around Ahiankwo (Emohua, Rivers). The bus was traveling from Port Harcourt to Akuku-Toru Local Council.
On 17 January 2022, a policeman shot and wounded a trailer driver in the Gombe-Darazo expressway, Dukku LGA (Gombe) during a stop and search operation. The victim was taken to the hospital.
On 14 May 2020, a mob of 3 tortured and injured a cleric in Amaseri (Afikpo North LGA, Ebonyi) over comments posted on Facebook.

Around 19 July 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight during a raid on their enclaves in the Azzara Forest, coded to Gidan Azara (Kachia, Kaduna). The militiamen fled and abandoned some rustled cows. The troops recovered several cows. There were no fatalities.

On 19 March 2024, para-athletes in Kwara state protested at the office of the state governor in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) over the failure of the governor to redeem some pledges he made to them prior to the participation in the 2023 national sports festival. The protesters also demanded for employment from the state government.
On 10 February 2021, ISWAP clashed with Nigerian troops between Mainok (Kaga LGA, Borno) and Jakana (Bama LGA, Borno), killing seven Nigerian soldiers and seizing weapons and ammunition.

On 19 June 2023, youths from Oduoha community protested at the premises of a radio station in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) over the murder of a naval rating by EMOLVICE operatives [coded separately]. The protesters demanded for justice for the victim.

On 24 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked worshippers at a mosque in Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The Imam and another worshipper were killed, many others were wounded. Other sources report that three persons were killed, two others were seriously wounded and that the assailants who were dressed in military uniform emerged from Kamuku forest and were en route to Tegina axis of Niger state.

Around 24 January 2021 (as reported), a Niger communal militia attacked and looted Paikoro and Munya Local Government Areas in Niger State, carting away spare parts, foodstuff and livestock and killing at least five residents. Militiamen also abducted about 15 female residents. Fatalities split across two events.

On 11 February 2021, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed a farmer at Igangan (Ibarapa North LGA, Oyo). Fulani pastoralists also set ablaze his cocoa farm in the area. Event connected to farmer-pastoralist conflict.

On 30 June 2024, police forces, DSS operatives and hunters trailed an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Gauraka forest (Suleja, Niger) after the group attacked civilians in Bwari (coded separately). Two out of four abductees were rescued, the assailants fled with gunshot injuries.

On 1 March 2021, an unidentified armed group numbering at least 100 attacked a police divisional headquarters in Essien Udim LGA (Akwa Ibom) coded to Ikot Ebak. The assailants set the police station, motorcycles and vehicles ablaze, there were no casualties.
On 27 March 2023, a Katsina militia attacked policemen between Dan Musa and Maidabino village (Dan-Musa, Katsina). One policeman and one militiaman were killed.
On 25 March 2022, a policeman stabbed and killed two civilians in Yelwa (Bauchi, Bauchi). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 28 July 2021, unidentified gunmen beheaded two residents of Okporo (Orlu LGA, Imo state). Reports state that the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 28 August 2023, policemen arrested over 100 men at a hotel in (Warri South, Delta) coded to Warri over suspicion that they were holding a gay wedding ceremony.

On 14 November 2021, a Katsina militia clashed with the police at Danmarabu village (Kankara, Katsina), coded as Kankara, as the group attacked Gidan Duka village and rustled unspecified number of cattle. The group fled, leaving all animals.
On 24 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted two siblings from a residence in Damba coded and spelled as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). No further details.

On 7 July 2021, commercial tricycle riders took to the streets in Potiskum (Potiskum LGA, Yobe) in a demonstration over, what they stated, is the harassment by the Yobe State Road Traffic Agency (YOROTA).
On 3 October 2020, PDP militia members killed an APC party member near the Oba Adeshida Road in Akure (Akure South LGA, Ondo).

On 30 December 2023, women and youths from Ovwian community (Udu, Delta) protested along the community's main road against the recently held community executives election. The protesters claimed that irregularities characterized the whole process.
On 19 March 2020, suspected Fulani militias killed a farmer in Lowa (Ihitte-Uboma LGA, Imo).

On 15 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditional ruler of Riruwai community from his palace, coded to Lame district (Toro, Bauchi). The assailants shot sporadically in the air to scare away residents, and the abductee's corpse was recovered by a search party and there were no ransom demands. (coded separately).
On 14 July 2020, presumed ISWAP/ boko haram militants attacked civilians along the Government Day Secondary School axis in Gwoza LGA (Borno). Casualties unknown.

On 15 January 2022, unidentified armed individuals attacked a police station and were repelled by policemen at Mgbidi (Oru West, Imo). One policeman was killed, another sustained bullet wounds while the assailants fled while being pursued by police operatives.
On 1 October 2020, supporters of the Coalition for Revolution demonstrated at in Benin City (Oredo LGA, Edo) against bad governance in support of the #RevolutionNow Movement.
On 4 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SEC militia clashed in Atan (Ado-Odo, Ogun). One person was killed.
On 2 July 2020, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Njiboli village (Yola-South, Adamawa) coded as Karewa, and invaded a residence. One person was wounded and another was abducted.

Around 9 April 2024 (as reported), the Hybrid forces comprising the military, police, and State Security Service, in conjunction with CJTF, ambushed and killed four Boko Haram (JAS) fighters along Dikwa- Gajibo road, coded to Gajibo (Dikwa, Borno). The troops recovered food items and other logistic materials.

On 10 July 2023, an unidentified armed group of six were engaged in an armed clash by policemen and hunters at Fere village (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode after they attempted to abduct a civilian. Two members of the group were killed and the others fled.
On 25 May 2021, a Sokoto communal militia attacked Magira village in Gatawa (Sabon Birni LGA, Sokoto) and killed the village head. Unknown reason for attack.
Around 20 August 2020 (as reported), ISWAP elements attacked Nigerian troops in Ngwom (Mafa LGA, Borno).

On 22 September 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted four others along the Isan-Iye Ekiti road, coded to Iye (Ilejemeji, Ekiti). The police later rescued the four hostages.

On 5 June 2023, mourners who were headed to a funeral clashed with operatives of Operation Safe Haven at a checkpoint in Mararaban Jama'a (Jos South, Plateau). One person was killed; other sources report two fatalities and two others were wounded by the operatives, their vehicle was set ablaze by the mob, the clash was over a disagreement on the protocol of passing the through the checkpoint.

On 27 July 2020, suspected Nasarawa Communal Militia attacked Dawusu village in Toto LGA (Nasarawa), killing five and burning fifteen houses. Fourteen other residents, including a retired DSS officer were abducted.

On 3 May 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a journalist at the state government house in Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano). The victim is a correspondent at the state house, the state government denied that he was shot and claimed that he was hit by metal debris from a construction site within the government house.

Around 8 April 2021 (as reported), the Nigerian Airforce conducted airstrikes against ISWAP fighters at Kusuma (Ngala LGA), Sigir (Ngala LGA), and Arijallamari, also called Ali-Jilamari (Abadam LGA), in Borno State, killing dozens of ISWAP fighters in addition to two commanders. 14 fatalities split across three events.
On 14 February 2021, unidentified gunmen abducted at least 21 passengers at Kundu Village along Zungeru road (Wushishi LGA, Niger). All victims were later released. Unclear if ransom was paid.

On 9 June 2020, Longuda and Waja Ethnic militias clashed in Mamsirme, Boshikiri, Zakawon and Burtil in Lamurde LGA (Adamawa) over the ownership of farmland. 23 people were killed, houses and propery destroyed and 32 people arrested by Police forces. Fatalities split between 3 events.

Around 28 February 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be illegal miners ambushed soldiers and forest guards at Ifumkpa community (Akamkpa, Cross River), coded to Akankpa. One rifle belonging to the forest guards was destroyed, casualties unknown.
On 6 June 2020, Adara militiamen killed a community member in Kallah (Kajuru LGA, Kaduna) for the alleged cooperation with Fulani militias.

On 21 August 2023, two rival Benue militia engaged in an armed clash at Chito (Ukum, Benue) and continued the clash the following day [coded separately]. Five persons were killed; the market was also set ablaze by the assailants, other sources report that four persons were killed in Chito and one was killed in the suburbs.

On 8 July 2024, soldiers abducted two civilians from the Kelebe area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) when they stormed a gathering of Kelebe-Omu Landlord Association members who had gathered to enforce a court judgement.

On 1 December 2023, hundreds of Imo women protested at the INEC State headquarters in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) over the delay in releasing the certified true copies (CTC) of the governorship election. The women dressed in black attires were drawn from the three senatorial areas of the state. They lamented the delay had caused anguish for the people.

Around 23 April 2021 (as reported), the Icelander cult group shot and killed 4 people in Ajakajak, Samanga, Ibute-Irem and Dema, coded to Ngo (Andoni, Delta). The militants invaded the communities on about ten speed boats and shot sporadically, forcing the residents to flee for safety. 4 casualties reported.

On 7 August 2021, police forces of Nigeria clashed with an unidentified armed group in a kidnap attempt at Ibeshe, (Egbado North LGA, Ogun state). A Swiss expatriate and his driver were kidnapped, three people were reported killed and one wounded in the clash.
On 19 September 2021, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at the Zunuruk Agban community in Kagoro axis (Kaura, Kaduna). No other details. Casualties unknown.
On 24 August 2021, protesters in support of Uche Secondus protested at secretariat of the PDP in Wuse (Abuja Municipal, FCT) demanding that he continue as the party chairman.

On 15 August 2024, the APC youth group protested around the secretariat in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue) over the party's leadership crisis in the state. They decried the existence of the Agada factional leadership and lamented the faction undermined the authority of the state governor, who by default is the state's party leader. The protesters vowed not to allow any factional member access to the party's secretariat. The protest disrupted vehicular movement in the city.

On 17 November 2023, the air component of Operation Haderin Daji launched air strikes on the Katsina militia's enclave in Dan Musa LGA, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). Several militiamen were killed, and various structures were destroyed. Fatalities coded as 3.
On 3 November 2022, Nigerian troops fired artillery shells in the vicinity of Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.
On 27 December 2020, unidentified gunmen attacked Nagu village (Katsina-Ala LGA, Benue), killing at least three residents. Unknown reason for attack.

Around 7 May 2021 (as reported), a Niger communal militia attacked Yangalu community (Magama LGA, Niger) [coded to Nasko] and killed seven residents. Property damage also reported. Unknown reason for attack.
On 18 October 2023, a Kaduna militia ambushed a team of hunters and killed one while they were conducting a highway patrol along Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 17 July 2021, the Aye and Eiye cult groups clashed in Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos) over the control of the territory. During the clash, ten members of the Aye confraternity pursued and shot an Eiye member dead at point-blank range. 1 fatality reported.

Property destruction: On 9 July 2023, an unidentified armed group vandalized the secretariat of the SDP and burned some materials in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The party's deputy governorship candidate claimed that the vandals were suspected to have been sponsored. Other sources report that the party claimed that the attack was sponsored by the state government while the state government denied the claims.

On 14 February 2021, Nigerian military forces conducted airstrikes against Boko Haram fighters in Egiri, Zira 1 and 2 villages in Biu LGA (Borno), following an attack in the area by BH. No reported fatalities.

Weapons seizure: On 2 June 2021, police dismantled an illegal weapons factory in Jos South LGA (Plateau) [coded to Bukuru]. 2 people were arrested and over 20 pieces of locally-produced AK-47 rifles were seized.

On 9 December 2023, policemen were engaged in armed clash with an unidentified armed group when they invaded their hideout in the bush at Egbudu-Akah (Aniocha South, Delta). The group fled and left an abductee behind, one member of the group was killed as a result of bullet wounds that he sustained.
Property destruction: Around 20 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified assailants set fire to the Ikwuano High Court, coded to Isiala Oboro (Ikwuano, Abia).

On 13 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one person and forced others to flee after invading a Christian community near Chibok, coded to Chibok (Chibok, Borno). The militia stole unspecified property.

On 1 August 2024, residents demonstrated in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) against the hike of fuel prices, using the hashtag #EndBadGovernanceInNigeria. The police fired tear gas to disperse them.

On 18 March 2024, a civil society group called Rights for Human Dignity and Justice protested at Trans Amadi area (Port Harcourt, Rivers) to demand for the arrest and prosecution of the secretary general of NUPENG over claims of court contempt.
Around 2 October 2024 (as reported), suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted an Igbaja resident and later killed him on the Ogele-Yaaru road near Igaja (Ifelodun, Kwara).
On 14 November 2020, a mob attacked presumed policemen, who responded by opening fire and killing two, at Sharada area of Gwale LGA (Kano). Motivation for the attack in unknown/not reported.
On 7 September 2021, armed militia abducted eighteen people from Keke community (Chikun, Kaduna), coded to Chikun. There are no reports for ransom demands yet.
Around 14 July 2020 (as reported), Boko Haram ambushed a military convoy at Kongiri, near Mainok (Kaga LGA, Borno). 4 soldiers were killed and military equipment looted.
On 11 May 2023, the family of a taxi driver who was murdered by a local defense militia protested in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) against his murder. The protesters also demanded for justice.
On 28 October 2022, a Katsina militia abducted 4 people from Funtua in the vicinity of Jabiri (Funtua, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 5 March 2020, suspected Fulani militias attacked Mbanyiar in the Mbawa ward of Guma LGA (Benue), looted the village, raped women and attacked the district head.

On 9 January 2021, ISWAP ambushed Nigerian troops between Maiduguri (Maiduguri LGA, Borno) and Mafa (Mafa LGA, Borno), allegedly killing a number of soldiers and seizing weapons and ammunition. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 November 2020, members of the Islamic Movement of Nigeria staged protest marches at NITEL Junction and Wuse Market in Abuja (Abuja Municipal LGA, FCT) against French President Emmanuel Macron's comments over the republishing of caricatures of Prophet Muhammed in a magazine.

On 8 July 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged in armed clash with soldiers at Tine-Nune community on the Zaki Biam-Wukari road (Ukum, Benue) after they fled from the villages where they attacked civilians at Zaki Akpunna I and Diom [coded separately]. Casualties are unknown.
Around 19 March 2021 (as reported), a Kaduna communal militia attacked Masaka village (Chikun LGA, Kaduna) but were repelled by Nigerian military troops. One reported fatality and two injuries.

On 22 April 2021, Hausa residents set bonfires at New Artisan Market along Enugu/Port-Harcourt Expressway (Enugu North LGA, Enugu) over the demolishment of their community by Nigerian security operatives. Demonstrators also vandalized property. Police forces fired live ammunition in an attempt to disperse the crowd. Reported injuries.

On 3 August 2024, youths clashed with the police while demonstrating against alleged bad governance in Unguwa Uku (Tarauni, Kano), Kurna, Rijiyar Lemo, Bachirawa, Danwanau and Kofar Nassarawa area, coded separately. The demonstrators defied the curfew (imposed due to violent demonstrations on the previous day) and marched on the streets. It was alleged that the demonstrators attempted to burn the Rijiyar Lemo police station and exploit the march to loot shops. The police teargassed them, injured many, and shot at least eight dead. The demonstrators pelted stones at the police and injured a Police officer. Eight fatalities shared across six events; 1 fatality coded.

On 2 August 2021, Fulani herders attacked Kwall Central in Miango (Bassa LGA, Plateau state). The attack led to the death of at least 10 people, the displacement of over 15,000 persons and destruction of houses.
On 7 October 2021, ISWAP claimed a clash with Nigerian troops and CJTF militia in Mandafuma (Biu, Borno); according to the claim, one CJTF member was killed and the troops fled.
On 21 April 2022, unidentified armed individuals shot and killed a Fulani pastoralist in Rangyel community, Bassa LGA (Plateau). Four cows were killed and five others were wounded.
On 26 June 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted three farmers from Taka-Lafiya and rustled 60 cows from Gidan-Makeri in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). There are no reports on ransom demands.
Around 22 August 2020 (weekend of), Sokoto Communal Militias abducted a yet-to-be ascertained number of traders along Balle-Tangaza Road (Tangaza LGA, Sokoto).

On 28 March 2021, a Kaduna militia shot and killed a security guard when he tried to alert local defense militias about the attack in Lalighi community, coded to nearby Goni Gora (Chikun, Kaduna). One person was injured, four others, including the wife and two children of an employee of Defence Industries Corporation, were abducted. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 8 September 2020, residents, along with members of NANS, protested on major streets in Akure (Akure South LGA, Ondo) over the increase in fuel prices and electricity tariffs.

On 25 November 2021, four monarchs from Ilejemeji led their communities to protest against the partial implementation of the supreme court's judgement about the relocation of council headquarters. Location coded as Iye (Ilejemeje, Ekiti).

On 24 October 2023, a joint team of soldiers and DSS operatives engaged a Boko Haram militant in an armed clash when they raided his residence at Gbaganu area of Minna (Minna, Niger). The militant fled; 150 AK 47 rifles, 20 rocket propellers and 3000 live ammunition were recovered by the security agents, occupants of the house including women and children were arrested.

On 21 October 2020, ISWAP militants attacked a Nigerian Army Base in Magumeri (Magumeri LGA, Borno) but were repelled by Nigerian troops. Eleven Boko Haram militants were reportedly killed and weapons and ammunition recovered.

On 20 March 2022, Nigerian soldiers repelled an attack by Sokoto militiamen on traders along Sokoto-Goronyo road (Goronyo, Sokoto). The militiamen blocked the road with the intention of robbing and abducting traders; casualties unknown.
On 8 November 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted a catholic priest at Kurmin Sara (Kachia, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 25 July 2021, an unidentified armed group attacked and abducted civilians along the Wurno-Goronyo road, Wurno (Sokoto state). Two people were killed and an unspecified number of people were abducted.
On 28 January 2021, unidentified gunmen attacked Kungi village in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna), killing one resident and abducting 30 others. Unknown reason for attack.

On 31 July 2021, demonstrators obstructed the APC ward congress in Iremo Ward 1 and Ilare Ward 4 (Ife Central LGA, Osun state) coded as Ile-Ife. They attempted to chase away party members from collation centers.

Around 4 March 2023 (as reported), suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians and killed over 50 farmers at 12 communities in Kwande LGA (Benue) including Moon, Mbaikyor, Mbadura, Ilyav and Ugbe. Scores of other persons were persons sustained varying degrees of injuries, houses and barns were burned in the attack which lasted for 4 days [coded separately]. 50 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 10.

Around 30 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops from Benue and Taraba clashed with armed Fulani militiamen at Kashimbila (Takum, Tarab) during a patrol. One militiaman was killed, the others fled with varying degrees of wounds and left a teenager boy behind. The troops set the militia's makeshift camp ablaze and recovered 4 cutlasses, one knife and other weapons.
On 19 December 2020, a female Boko Haram suicide bomber killed three people in Konduga (Konduga LGA, Borno). It is unclear whether this figure included the bomber.

Around 23 May 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia killed one man who they abducted alongside others on the Wawa-Luma road (Borgu, Niger) over the failure of his family to pay the demanded 2 million naira ransom within 48 hours. The victim was killed after the ransom was paid because it was delivered late.
On 27 April 2021, an unidentified cult militia attacked a shawarma hotspot and killed one person at the polytechnic community in or around Oghara (Ethiope West, Delta).
On 1 March 2020, unidentified gunmen attacked multiple villages, including Kerawa, in Igabi LGA (Kaduna), killing 51 residents in total. Fatalities split between 4 events.
On 14 November 2020, a mob killed a suspected thief in Afiesere community (Ughelli North, Delta).

Around 18 November 2023 (between 18 - 19 November), the Nigerian troops engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight in Dan Musa LGA, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina) and Malumfashi LGA. They also engaged the militia in Maru LGA, in Zamfara State, coded separately. The troops recovered one AK47 rifle with a magazine loaded with 13 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammo, 3 mobile phones, one motorcycle and the sum of N18,560.00'. Two hostages were released, and four militiamen were killed in the three operations. 4 fatalities shared among the three events. 1 fatality coded.
Around 6 April 2021 (as reported), unidentified gunmen clashed with Nigerian police operatives in Dogongawa along Katsina Ala -Takum road (Takum LGA, Taraba), killing two policemen.

On 1 January 2023, a mob attacked a policeman and a tow truck driver using sledge hammer, sticks and other weapons at an accident scene in Orile Imo (Obafemi, Ogun). The policeman had gone to inspect the accident, and the rioters were trying to prevent investigation; 520,000 naira was stolen from the tow truck that was set ablaze by the mob and the victims sustained varying degrees of injuries. Three of the rioters were arrested, the others fled.

Non-violent activity: On 25 June 2022, police operatives rescued an abductee after they set up patrols which led the unidentified armed group that abducted him to flee along Ezinifite road, Aguata (Aguata, Anambra). The assailants abandoned their operational vehicle and the victim's vehicle which they stole.

Property destruction: On 11 November 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to have been sponsored by the APC destroyed campaign billboards of the LP house of representatives candidate for Anka, Omala and Olamaboro federal constituency at Okpo, Ikeje (Olamaboro, Kogi), Ibana and other locations [coded separately]. The LP candidate claimed that the assailants threatened his supporters with arms and ammunition which caused them to flee.

Around 26 September 2022 (between 23 September - 26 September), the air component of Operation Hadin Kai carried out airstrikes against ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at Bukar Meram (Monguno, Borno) and Koloram [coded separately]. Several militants were killed and their structures were destroyed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 2 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia dressed in military and police uniforms abducted four persons who were returning from the farm at Mgbuji-Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 22 July 2024, IS/Boko Haram fighters opened fire indiscriminately in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). A woman was shot and injured.

On 2 August 2022, suspected Black Axe also called Aiye/ Eiye cult militias killed a commercial tricycle operator whom they trailed to where he went to eat in Agboyi area of Alapere (Kosofe, Lagos). The victim was shot in the head, before his body was cut machete, the assailants cut his hand and took it away. The attack was a result of an ongoing clash between Eiye and Black Axe militias. The assailants covered their faces with handkerchiefs and escaped, residents claim that the police arrested innocent persons in connection with the attack. Two other person were killed on different days [coded separately], the police claimed only 2 persons were killed and some persons were abducted in connection with the attack.

Displacement: Around 21 August 2021 (as reported), over 50,000 residents have fled 17 communities in Sabon Birni, (Sabon Birni, Sokoto) due to ttacks by armed militias. They are currently taking refuge in Maradi, Niger Republic.

On 26 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a pastor an dumped his corpse near Malkohi IDP camp in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The victim was abducted the previous day from his house, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 7 May 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from Evbohen quarters in the Idumebo community, coded to Abudu (Orhionwon, Edo). The abductors collected N9 million but later killed the victim on the same day.

On 7 July 2023, operatives of Operation Rainbow and a Mwaghavul ethnic militia attacked over eight Fulani settlements in Mangu LGA (Plateau) as claimed by MACBAN. 15 pastoralists were killed, 78 hamlets were razed and over 2000 cows and several other livestock were missing. MACBAN added that the operatives attacked in an armored tank while the militia set the hamlets ablaze.
On 6 February 2020, a women's organization demonstrated in Abuja (Abuja LGA, FCT) over police brutality against activists.
On 25 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed an EMOLVICE member and two civilians at Ubimini (Emohua, Rivers). The other victims included a pregnant woman, several houses were also burnt.

On 13 January 2022, unidentified armed individuals abducted four students of the federal university Lafia from the university community in Mararaba, Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). The victims were rescued by security operatives around 17 January.

On 18 March 2020, Nigerian Air Force conducted air strikes against a meeting venue of ISWAP in Alinwa in the Lake Chad area (Borno, ) and killed commanders and fighters of the group. Structures of the camp were destroyed. Unknown number of fatalities coded as 10.

Around 30 April 2021 (as reported), Nigerian police clashed with a Kaduna communal militia at Kudenda in Sabon Gari (Chikun LGA, Kaduna) following a distress call about their kidnapping activities in the area. Security operatives rescued three out of four kidnapped victims.

On 28 January 2023, a member of Ebube Agu corps killed his colleague in Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi) following a disagreement over 1000 naira and the sharing formula of money given to them during a campaign rally of the All Progressives Congress. The victim had attempted to shoot the assailant first but the assailant was quicker to act. Other sources report that the altercation was over other reasons while the state Ebube Agu commander claimed that the assailant was not a member of the corps but a member of an unidentified armed group.

On 17 November 2022, a soldier shot and killed another soldier and a humanitarian worker in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The assailant also stabbed one helicopter pilot before he was shot and killed by other soldiers.

On 19 March 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded some INEC officials when they invaded the collation center at Ogoja (Ogaja, Cross River). The assailants also destroyed duplicate result sheets and a laptop.
On 10 December 2021, drivers blocked the Mokwa by Zugurma road, Mokwa LGA (Niger) while protesting over the killing of a motorist by a soldier.

On 7 September 2023, a mob attacked and attempted to lynch some DSS operatives who had shot and wounded a tailor and a sales girl in Garki Ultramodern Market, Garki (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The DSS shot the tailor while trying to arrest him for failure to deliver a sewing job given to him by a lady, coded separately. The police intervened and rescued the DSS officers, and the mobs damaged a section of the police outpost.

On 8 February 2023, troops of 1 Division in collaboration with the air component of Operation Whirl stroke clashed with a Kaduna militia and cleared Manini-Kuriga, Farin Ruwa, Kwanan Yashi, Makera, Dogon Dawa-Maidaro, Kidandan-Yadi and Sabon Birnin in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna) and Giwa LGA [coded separately]. The operation lasted for about 48 hours; 4 militiamen were killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds, one loaded rifle and six motorcycles were recovered by the troops. 4 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 1.

On 6 June 2023, youths and majority of the state house of assembly members protested in Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa) against the suspension of the state house of assembly inaugration by the governor. The protesters were also against the imposition of an unpopular candidate as the speaker of the house.

On 17 April 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired several mortar shells and killed civilians in Goniri (Gujba, Yobe). An unspecified number of persons were wounded in the attack which was the militants' response to a failed attempt to attack the town. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 23 November 2021, suspected IPOB militants attacked and razed down a police station in Ndizuogu (Ideato North, Imo). One policeman was killed in the attack, machete cuts were inflicted on the head of another officer, one police vehicle and the personal car of an officer were also burnt.

On 15 October 2024, a Sokoto militia killed the Chief Imam of Subarru while returning from the hospital in the Subarru community, location coded to the nearest populated area, Dange (Dange-Shuni, Sokoto). The Imam was together with his wife when the militia killed him.

On 3 April 2022, an armed group attacked and killed two FRSC officials on duty along the Igbo-Ukwu-Ezinifite-Uga link road (Aguata, Anambra). One official escaped into the bush and one other sustained severe injuries from the attack.

On 17 November 2020, Kaduna militiamen attacked the Nigerian Defence Academy in Jaji (Igabi, Kaduna), one officer sustained gunshot wound. The militiamen also shot a motorist (fatality or injury unknown) long the road of the college.

On 10 November 2023, the Nigerian troops repelled the Boko Haram (JAS) in a attempt to invade Damboa from the Gwoza axis in Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The ensuing firefights forced the militia to retreat. There were no fatalities.

Around 9 May 2024 (between 7 May - 11 May), a Zamfara militia killed three civilians at Yarsabaya (Anka, Zamfara) and 46 others in Dangulbi, Duhuwa, Tsatsomawa, and Farar-Kasa (coded separately). The attacks lasted from 7 to 11 May.

On 23 November 2022, a mob attacked and beat up a fireman with machetes at Okujagu slaughter market in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim who was wounded an taken to a hospital was attacked because the mob was offended that the firemen responded late to a fire emergency at the market.

On 22 September 2023, the Giyawa community residents attacked the suspected informant of the Sokoto militia and killed him in Giyawa (Goronyo, Sokoto). They alleged the victim was an informant of the militia who killed four people and abducted others in their community.

On 17 June 2021, ISWAP fighters clashed with Nigerian police operatives following an attack on Gujba town (Gujba LGA, Yobe). At least three policemen were killed. ISWAP fighters also looted medical supplies and set properties and houses ablaze.
On 19 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditional ruler of Idofin and his wife along Makutu-Idofin road (Yagba East, Kogi). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 12 July 2024, ISWAP militants killed two people and abducted six others in Morai village in Mobbar LGA, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). They demanded a five million naira ransom for their release.

On 16 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed on civilian and wounded several others along Edem-Nrobo-Ezikolo-Abbi road (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The assailants laid seige on the road for several hours.
On 5 September 2022, pensioners protested and marched from the union house to the government house in Minna (Minna, Niger) over their unpaid pensions and gratuities.

On 18 January 2022, suspected Isinkwo militiamen attacked and killed four persons from Ukawu at Okuzu-Ukawu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The attack is related to a protracted dispute between the two communities; the state government claimed that the attack was carried out by abaomege militiamen with the aim of causing collusion between the other communities.

On 26 August 2021, a military aircraft shot at a boat conveying passengers near Dutch Island in Okrika (Okrika, Rivers), wounding three civilians and an unspecified number were killed, coded as 3. The reason for the attack is not reported, military sources have not made a statement yet.

On 7 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a former Nassarawa state deputy governor when they invaded Gwagi village in Wamba LGA (Nassarawa) and shot sporadically before taking the abductee away. The abductors fled with the victim before the arrival of policemen, the abductee was released on 9 April after a ransom of 4 million naira was paid.

On 15 September 2024, ISWAP fighters attacked the Bakoura-led Boko Haram (JAS) in the Gurnuwa and Laraba Mairari areas of Lake Chad Basin Marte LGA, location coded to local administrative headquarters, Marte (Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed in the confrontation, and weapons were recovered. Unknown casualties coded as 10.
Around 13 May 2020 (as reported), police forces raided a training camp of IPOB in Okpanam (Oshimili North LGA, Delta) and seized weapons.
On 13 October 2020, hundreds of #EndSARS supporters, including women, gathered at Pleasure Park in Port Harcourt (Port-Harcourt LGA, Rivers) to protest against police brutality across the country.

On 20 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a fisher after he refused them from grazing on the farmlands around his fishing camp, one farmer also sustained gunshot wounds. Location coded to Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa).

Displacement: Around 28 September 2023 (as reported), the Shapai Village people fled their community, about 15 kilometres from Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger), after the Communal Militia occupied their home. The village sought refuge in the neighbouring communities.

On 2 August 2023, thousands of workers, the chairman of the NLC and the deputy governor of Niger state protested in Minna (Minna, Niger) and marched from the labor house to the state house of assembly over the removal of fuel subsidy. The protesters also demanded for attention to be given to the security situation in the state.

Property destruction: On 24 November 2021, Bayan-Men attacked and set fire to the Onosi-Ogu manifold facility, operated by the Nigerian AGIP oil company, in the Obosi area (Ogba LGA, Rivers), coded to Omoku.
On 26 February 2020, unidentified gunmen attacked Tsabuwa in Kankara LGA (Katsina) and killed an unreported number of residents. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
Around 25 March 2021 (as reported), Nigerian military clashed with a Kaduna communal militia in the Buruku axis (Chikun LGA, Kaduna), killing two and destroying their structures.

On 26 July 2023, a Zamfara militia were repelled by soldiers when they invaded Talata Mafara town (Talata Mafara, Zamfara) and abducted 10 staff of a construction company from their houses. The militiamen operated in the town for one and a half hour before they were repelled. Other sources report that one boy was injured, 12 persons were abducted and four of them escaped.
Looting: On 11 March 2022, armed individuals looted 7 cows in Yammama (Malumfashi, Katsina).

On 22 January 2021, the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) security outfit, Eastern Security Network (ESN), clashed with Nigerian Military troops at Okporo (Orlu LGA, Imo). IPOB sources report five civilians were killed, while community and government sources report one person was killed. Property damage also reported. Attack related to government directive to dismantle the formation of the ESN in the area.

On 24 June 2022, Niger militiamen ambushed members of a local self defense militia from Abaji and hunters who were on a rescue mission some kilometers from Lafia Kpada-Doma (Lapai, Niger). Two NSVC members, three self defense militiamen from FCT and one of farmers who was abducted from Doma [coded separately] were killed, six other self defense militiamen were wounded.
On 29 January 2020, hundreds of students of the Delta State Polytechnic in Ozoro (Isoko North LGA, Delta) demonstrated at their campus over the conditions at their institution.

On 19 February 2024, hundreds of protesters mostly youth, protested in Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo) over the economic situation of the country and demanded for the government's intervention. The protesters marched to major areas of the city including Mokola, Bodija, and Agodi (coded separately).

On 10 March 2021, members of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) staged demonstrations at Amarata, the House of Assembly and the State Secretariat in Yenegoa (Yenegoa LGA, Bayelsa) over the removal of the minimum wage bill from the exclusive list to the concurrent list.

On 1 January 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with hunters clashed with Boko Haram [JAS] militants who abducted two civilians in the axis of Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The militants abandoned the abductees and fled.

On 11 April 2023, youths from Nimo protested in Nimo (Njikoka, Anambra) against the sale of a large parcel of the land in the community. Security operatives comprised of policemen, soldiers, NSCDC operatives and a local defense militia numbering up to 100 disrupted the protest and insisted that the protesters did not receive due clearance to carry out the protest.

Around 21 September 2023 (week of), the Niger Communal Militia abducted 21 people from the villages around Munya LGA, coded to Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). They kept the hostages in the temporary camp in Tsohon Kabula.

Around 28 May 2021 (as reported), suspected Fulani pastoralists clashed with local militiamen following an attack on Na'ikko village (Giwa LGA, Kaduna), killing three residents. Following the attack, youths of Na'ikko village invaded a Fulani settlement in Rugan Abdulmuminu (Giwa LGA, Kaduna) and killed two residents in a reprisal attack.

Around 1 April 2022 (as reported), soldiers on a clearance operation engaged over 400 Niger militiamen in an armed clash near Zuma Barrack, coded to nearby Suleja (Suleja, Niger). 14 soldiers and several militiamen were killed, several other soldiers were wounded. Several militia men deaths coded as 3. Fatalities coded as 17.

On 2 August 2022, a Fulani militia killed one person and abducted 2 other people in Manchok (Kaura, Kaduna). The assailants shot sporadically before abducting people; the abductees were the rector of the federal school of statistics, and the grand daughter of the murdered victim, they were released after 1 million naira was paid for the rector and 150 thousand naira was paid for the girl. The abductee claimed the assailants were young Fulani men.

On 26 February 2023, voters protested outside a collation center at Marina (Lagos Island, Lagos) over claims that they were disenfranchised and demanded to be allowed to vote. The protesters sang solidarity songs and chanted 'we must vote'.
On 9 June 2020, militias from Isinkwo community attacked Abba-Omega (Onicha LGA, Ebonyi) over a land dispute. 1 person was killed, 3 abducted and 10 injured.

On 24 July 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked troops of Operation Hadarin Daji and engaged them in an armed clash at Kango Sabuwal village in Wanke district (Gusau, Zamfara). Seven militiamen were killed, one machine gun, ammunition and 6 motorcycles were recovered by the troops when they repelled the attack.

On 10 March 2021, unidentified gunmen invaded the National Institute of Construction Technology in Uromi (Esan North East LGA, Edo), abducting three students and staff. Kidnapped victims were later released. Reason for abduction unknown.

On 8 May 2022, hundreds of APC members in Ilesa West LGA protested at the residence of the party's state chairman in Igbona (Olorunda, Osun) against the consensus candidates chosen to demand that a primary election should be conducted to ascertain the choice of candidates for the state House of Assembly elections.
On 13 March 2020, suspected Fulani militias attacked Katsira in Gusau LGA (Zamfara) and engaged in a gun battle with Yansakai militias. Reports on Yansakai fatalities range between 4 and 11.

Around 22 May 2024 (as reported), police forces raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group, engaged them in an armed clash and killed an unspecified number of members of the armed group. The raid resulted from an ambush on policemen (coded separately), where 13 of their rifles were stolen. 10 of the rifles were recovered, location coded to Ohoro (Ughelli North, Delta) where the first ambush took place. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 4 January 2022, an unidentified armed group invaded a residence, killed an Islamic cleric and abducted his wife in the vicinity of Gidan Madara (Mubi South, Adamawa), coded as Gella.

Around 28 May 2023 (as reported), members of local defense militia killed a commercial tricycle rider at Ojoto community (Idemili South, Anambra) and stole his tricycle. The assailants including the militia's commander and two other members dumped the victim's body in a river and sold his tricycle, they were arrested by the police.

On 18 December 2023, a mob killed a man at Welepe Kujore area of Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). The reason for the attack is unknown, some sources report that the victim was mistaken for a robber and he was clubbed to death.
On 8 June 2020, Nigerian Armed Forces attacked a camp of Boko Haram at Kwatara in the Mandara Mountains in Gwoza LGA (Borno) and killed several fighters. Several fatalities coded 3.

On 14 January 2024, a Zamfara militia engaged a local defense militia and security operatives [coded as police forces] in an armed clash when they invaded Magizawa community in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). Three local defense militia members including a leader were killed, two to five others were wounded, 50 locals 36 of whom were women were abducted.

On 14 December 2022, IPOB militants from a faction led by Simon Ekpa who were enforcing a sit in order killed one person when they invaded Isinweke (Ihitte Uboma, Imo). The assailants burned several vehicles including commercial and private vehicles and motorcycles. An occupant of one of the vehicles was wounded.

On 21 December 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a medical doctor at his residence in Kanbi (Moro, Kwara) coded to Bode Saadu. The doctor's 16 year old daughter was also abducted by the assailants. Other sources report that the abductee was 23 years old.

On 5 August 2024, youths vandalized and looted public and private properties in Zaria (Zaria, Kaduna) over the high cost of living, hunger, and alleged bad governance in Nigeria. They demonstrated in the context of the #EndBadGovernanceInNigeria demonstrations. They waved Russian and Chinese flags, calling for a coup and support from Russia to overthrow President Tinubu. They set fire to the KASTLEA office in Zone 6, Zaria. Police teargassed and dispersed them.

On 21 September 2021, the Niger state chapter of the association of retired police officers protested in Minna (Minna, Niger). The protesters demanded better retirement benefits and an exemption from contributory pension scheme. The demonstration was organized by the Association of Retired Police Officers.

On 13 May 2024, members of the NLC and TUC protested at the headquarters of the Ibadan electricity distribution company in Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo) over the hike in electricity tariff, of which the protesters demanded a reversal.

On 9 November 2021, suspected Kaduna militiamen attacked and killed a retired NAF officer and his wife at his residence in Rigasa (Igabi, Kaduna). Other reports indicate that the attack was perpetrated by 'suspected assassins.'

On 24 November 2022, ASUU members of Federal University Dutsinma protested and marched in the university's campus in Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina) against the no work no pay policy of the federal government and the non-payment of their salaries during the ASUU strike.

On 28 October 2022, a mob set the houses of some persons who were suspected to be involved in an abduction ablaze in Yantama (Doguwa, Kano) while demonstrating against the abduction of a boy in the area.

On 27 February 2024, a mob attacked two youths attempting to abduct one person with fake guns at Ngudo Burumma village in Damasak town (Mobbar, Borno). One of the suspects was killed, and the other escaped.

On 8 March 2023, troops of 13 Brigade Nigerian Army who were deployed to Operation Akpakwu ambushed an unidentified armed group at their hideout and engaged them in an armed clash around Peter Effiong Creek. The troops rescued the Cross River state commissioner for women affairs who was abducted by the group at Mayne Avenue [coded separately], while the members of the group fled. Location coded to Anantigha (Calabar South, Cross River) where the abduction was coded to.
On 15 January 2020, the Emir of Potiskum was attacked on the Kaduna-Zaria highway at Fandatio village (no location found, coded as Kaduna). 4 of his aides and 2 civilians were killed.

On 9 May 2024, Nigerian security forces, coded as the police and the local security guards, clashed with a Kogi militia who had abducted 24 students from Confluence University, Osara (Adavi, Kogi). The militia invaded the University at night while students were studying for an exam and opened fire sporadically. They abducted nine students before the intervention of security. There were no fatalities. 14 students were rescued after security agents engaged the assailants in an armed clash near Obajana on 12 May. 6 other students were rescued on 14 May.
On 8 November 2020, Nigerian military troops clashed with a Zamfara communal militia at Fegi Baza village (Tsafe LGA, Zamfara), killing two militiamen.

On 25 January 2022, policemen clashed with a group of unidentified armed individuals at Saala Orile forest (Egbado North, Ogun), coded as Aiyetoro, as they were attacking Fulani pastoralists. One policemen and two armed men were killed; the other members of the group fled with varying degrees of gunshot wounds. Guns, ammunition, a phone, one motorcycle and charms were recovered.

On 6 February 2023, protesters in their numbers under the aegis of Pro Nigeria group marched across different parts of Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT) in support of the Central Bank's policy on currency redesign.

On 17 May 2021, a coalition of widows and the next of kin of retired Primary school teachers staged a protest at the Government House in Uyo (Uyo LGA, Akwa Ibom) over the non-payment of their entitlements.
On 3 April 2022, an armed group killed seven persons and wounded 5 others in Tafi Gana village, Bassa (Plateau).

On 2 March 2021, members of the Federal Polytechnic Ado-Ekiti Chapter of the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP) staged a demonstration at the main entrance of the institution in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti LGA, Ekiti) over the non-payment of allowances and deductions by the management.
On 11 April 2021, a Katsina militia abducted 15 traders along Tsaskiya-Ummadau road (Safana LGA, Katsina). Reason for abduction unknown.

On 7 September 2022, Nigerian troops ambushed a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash around Fondisho area in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed and others escaped with bullet wounds.

On 12 January 2021, seven unidentified cult militias attacked and assaulted a man in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) after having an altercation with one of their members while queuing for national identity card registration. The armed militia dispossessed him of his phone and money, and the ensuing commotion disrupted the registration exercise.

On 13 October 2020, youth demonstrators staged various march protests at Badagry Roundabout, Badagry Local Government Secretariat, Akran Palace and Agbalata International Market in Badagry (Badagry LGA, Lagos) over the multiple checkpoints and extortion of motorists by law enforcement agents on the Agbara-Badagry Expressway.

On 1 January 2023, a mob attacked the convoy of the Sokoto state governor in Wamakko LGA (Sokoto), coded to Wamako, when he was returning from the PDP's gubernatorial rally. Two vehicles in the convoy were vandalized by the rioters who threw stones.
On 9 January 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed eight commuters in Kwapre, also called Kopre (Hong, Adamawa). No further details.

On 22 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked tipper drivers who were loading sand and wounded six of them at Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo). The assailants who were armed with guns and machetes also wounded a farmer whom they attacked with machetes on his farm.
On 7 July 2021, police officers killed one civilian in Oshimili South LGA (Delta) [coded to Asaba]. The circumstances of the event are unknown/not reported.
On 20 May 2024, an unidentified armed group clashed with DSS operatives at Zurak village, coded to New Zurak (Wase, Plateau) after the group attacked the area. Three members of the group were killed.

On 19 July 2022, workers from four tertiary institutions in Ondo state under the aegis of JAC protested in Akure (Akure South, Ondo) against poor funding of the institutions and non-payment of their salaries.

On 28 December 2021, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted 5 locals in Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu). There are no reports about demands for ransom. Fulani abducted 2 others at a different time between 22 - 27 December (coded separately).

On 28 May 2023, a policeman killed a civilian at the Oregun area of Ikeja (Ikeja, Lagos) when they shot sporadically while trying to disperse a crowd where people were fighting. The victim was hit by a stray bullet.

On 12 October 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked an operative of the police So Safe corps with a machete and wounded him at Anifowose community (Ifo, Ogun). The operatives had trailed the assailants who 10 in number when they stopped and attacked one operative. One motorcycle and a locally made gun were recovered by the operatives while the assailants fled.

Around 26 November 2020 (as reported), a Sokoto communal militia attacked residents of Deyeji village (Gudu LGA, Sokoto), killing one woman and setting houses ablaze. The attack may be a reprisal after local residents reported activities of militiamen to the Nigerian army.

On 29 December 2021, suspected members of a cult militia hired by a land speculator clashed with police forces during an attempt to assault a presidential aid in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). Police rescued the victim.

On 15 September 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a 21-year-old student at Ugbowo (Egor, Edo). The police rescued the hostage after trailing the abductors to their hideouts and engaged them in a firefight, coded separately.

On 5 October 2024, police attacked the officials of the River State Independent Electoral Commission at a polling unit in Elekahia (Port Harcourt, Rivers). They purportedly acted to implement the court order that restrained the electoral body from conducting the LGA election. They teargassed them and seized some electoral materials.

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three policemen who were on a stop and search duty by the Ole roundabout (Isoko South, Delta) and set the police van ablaze. It is unclear whether the assailants stole the policemen's rifles, other sources report that the rifles of the policemen were stolen and that the assailants were suspected armed robbers. Two out of the six assailants were arrested by the police.
On 25 May 2020, a security guard at a hotel in Bauchi (Bauchi LGA, Bauchi) was beaten to death by mob over a missing phone.

Around 9 June 2024 (as reported), troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted fighting patrols and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Dantarau community in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). 5 militia members were killed, weapons and ammunition were recovered.

On 25 August 2020, suspected ISWAP elements ambushed military troops along Monguno- Maiduguri road at Mairari Village (Guzamala LGA, Borno), but were repelled by troops. Reported injuries. Recovered weapons also reported.
On 14 May 2024, soldiers and Civilian JTF operatives clashed with Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants during a raid of Garin Fallujah in Bama LGA (Borno). Four militants were killed.

On 30 November 2022, hundreds of former Niger Delta agitators protested at the Presidential Amnesty office in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) over the removal of their names from the monthly stipend list which resulted in them not being paid for two months. The protesters also accused the management of shoddy deals.

Property destruction: Around 17 April 2024 (week of), Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai destroyed ISWAP/ Boko Haram strongholds at Ajigin (Damboa, Borno), Abulam, Buk, Dusula, Talala and Gorigi (locations coded separately).

On 8 August 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted ten members of a family in a suburb of Kaduna metropolis, coded to Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna). The hostages included the wife of a journalist and her two daughters, who were on holiday in the suburb.

On 27 July 2021, commercial motorcycle riders set tires on fire on roads in Isahudeen Junction Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) after a police officer killed a fellow motorcycle rider. The group also tried to enter the Governmental House, but security operatives (presumed police officers) dispersed the group.
On 8 September 2023, students of the nursing school protested in Gwadabawa town (Gwadabawa, Sokoto) over increased theft in the female hostels.

On 20 July 2024, the Nigerian troops of Operation UDO KA engaged IPOB in a firefight at Ezere Forest around Umuawa and Aku settlements in Okigwe, coded to Aku Ihube (Okigwe, Imo). IPOB fighters were overpowered and escaped with gunshot wounds. The military extended the offensive to Akawa Nnneato and Lomara communities in Umunneochi LGA, coded separately. The troops recovered one General Purpose Machine (GPM) gun and assorted rounds of ammunition, four motorcycles, and four radios. There were no fatalities.

On 30 January 2024, some youths burned down the house of the state Commissioner for Social Development and Gender in Ojah, spelt as Oja (Akoko Edo, Edo), over alleged denial of customary burial practice that involved corpses being left at the shrine or thrown into the hills around the community. The youth alleged that the king and the commissioner intended to stop the burial of a woman who was allegedly killed by the shrine and must be given the sky burial. They vandalized the king's palace and burned his SUV. They also stoned the security agencies trying to intervene in the crisis.

On 4 January 2022, Katsina militiamen attacked civilians in Makurdi, Bakori LGA (Katsina) and killed two persons, a health worker and a businessman. A woman and her two children were abducted in the attack.

On 1 December 2022, policemen guarding an INEC office repelled suspected IPOB militants that attempted to burn the office in Orlu (Orlu, Imo). The assailants invaded the area, shot sporadically and threw an IED which damaged the security post of the office before they were chased by the policemen. The police claimed that many of the assailants sustained serious wounds. IPOB denied any links to the attack and claimed that the government and police were trying to blackmail it by linking the groups with attacks.

On 1 August 2024, residents burned tires as they demonstrated in Dutse city (Dutse, Jigawa) against the hike of fuel prices, using the hashtag #EndBadGovernanceInNigeria. They also set ablaze the APC ruling party headquarters. The police fired tear gas and round bullets to disperse them, killing one.

On 7 November 2022, soldiers clashed with a Civilian JTF operative who was resisting arrest in the vicinity of Gana Ali stadium in Monguno LGA (Borno). One soldier and one Civilian JTF operative sustained bullet wounds.
On 27 December 2023, an unidentified armed group raped a 14-year old girl at Elekahia (Port Harcourt, Rivers) and threatened to kill her if she reported the incident.

On 29 January 2021, two unidentified cult militias clashed amongst each other at Aderogba, Bayerunka and Ogboriefon communities in Ibadan North East coded to Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). An unspecified number of shops and houses were looted and set on fire.

On 6 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a retired immigration officer whom they abducted around Ombi II in Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa) where they mounted a roadblock. The victim's body was found in the area the following morning.

On 6 January 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed three people in Molege community (Ose, Ondo), coded as Ifon. The assailants set farmlands and houses in the community ablaze after locals refused to permit the pastoralists to graze on their farms.
On 28 December 2021, Sokoto militiamen killed two people and abducted five others in Marakawa (Sabon Birni, Sokoto) [coded to Sabon Birni].

On 21 May 2024, the MNJTF convoy drove over an IED planted by ISWAP near the Doron Naira area of Lake Chad, coded to Doro Naira (Kukawa, Borno). An unspecified number of the MNJTF troops were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 10.

On 1 October 2024, a coalition of civil society organizations marched around Kings Square to the NUJ Press Centre in Benin City (Oredo, Edo), demanding the restoration of fuel subsidy, security improvement, and unicameral legislature in Nigeria. They decried the alleged harsh economic conditions and hunger in the country.

Around 27 June 2021 (as reported), IPOB militants killed a native doctor from Umudim Ukwu Orji Awo-Omamma (Oru East, Imo) for preparing ineffective charms for them. The victim was beheaded. Three other native doctors fled.
Looting: On 22 January 2024, a Sokoto militia stole an unspecified number of livestock along Meli village and Bakin Rafi in Gwadabawa LGA (Sokoto). They also shot sporadically in the process.

On 5 August 2020, Nigerian students under the JAC embarked on a peaceful protest at the NICON Junction in Maitama (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory) to demand the death sentence for corrupt public officials including other issues.

On 17 June 2021, Nigerian military and police with local Yansakai militiamen clashed with a Niger communal militia at Uddu, Rijau, Sabon Gari Ushe, and Warari communities (Rijau LGA, Niger). Reported fatalities. Suspects were also arrested. Unknown fatalities coded as 3. Fatalities split across four events.
On 28 September 2022, ISWAP claimed to have attacked an army checkpoint in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). Other sources denied the claims and insisted no attacks took place.
On 13 December 2020, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists injured a doctor in Ogoja (Ogaja, Cross River) during a kidnap attempt. The victim succeeded in escaping.

On 11 May 2020, a Niger militia attacked and shot indiscriminately in Kashua village Shiroro LGA (Niger), coded as Shiroro. The assailants had previously attacked Lakpma village, the casualties are unknown.
On 1 October 2021, students protested in Ile-Ife (Ife Central, Osun) over the death of their colleague due to alleged negligence of university authorities.

Around 2 September 2021 (as reported), Ediene and Ikot Ebak communities clashed and shot sporadically around Uyo-Ikot Abasi road, coded to Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). Casualties unknown. The road was blocked, and destruction was reported.

On 8 February 2023, soldiers attacked civilians, killed an unspecified number of people and set houses and other properties ablaze in Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra) over claims that their colleague was killed in a clash that occurred between Anaku and Omor. The soldiers demanded that the corpse of their colleague by produced. Fatalities coded as 3.
On 25 January 2021, ISWAP claimed an IED attack against Nigerian troops at Alagarno Forest (Biu LGA, Borno), killing and wounding several Nigerian soldiers. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 14 October 2021, thousands of basketball players protested over the alleged poor leadership of the Nigeria basketball federation in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT).

On 5 June 2023, a mob of suspected APC loyalists numbering over 100, who were armed with sticks and stones attacked and beat up a PDP chieftain at the entrance of the state election tribunal in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun).

On 18 April 2020, unidentified gunmen attacked villages in Dutsin Ma LGA (Katsina). 4 residents in Kurecin Giye, 6 residents in Kurecin Dutse, 19 residents in Makauwachi and 4 residents in Daule were killed.
On 31 March 2020 (or around), unidentified gunmen attacked Zoron Giwa in Sabon Birni LGA (Kaduna).
On 27 July 2020, Fulani militia attacked Zemadede and Tanlang villages in Langtang North LGA (Plateau), killing ten.

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group, suspected to have come from Mbayongo Council Ward, killed nine people in Anyom (Katsina Ala, Benue). The attack was suspected to be a result of a gang war. The militia burned many houses and destroyed other property. There were nine fatalities.

On 13 February 2023, troops of 152 battalion Banki of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives and hunters ambushed Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants at Banki (Bama, Borno). 8 militants were killed, 6 rifles, two motorcycles and other items were recovered.

On 9 March 2024, three soldiers dressed in plain clothes stabbed and killed an NDLEA operative at a checkpoint manned by NDLEA officials in Bida town (Bida, Niger). The attack resulted after the soldiers were searched at the checkpoint after which they returned with more men, killed the operative and took his rifle.

On 23 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen shot and killed an off duty Customs Operative in Rigacikun (Igabi, Kaduna) and abducted between four to five people. The customs operative died in the hospital from the gunshot wounds.

Around 16 February 2021 (as reported), four members of an unidentified cult militia attacked and gang-raped a girl in Ejigbo (Oshodi, Lagos). The militiamen armed with cutlasses waylaid the girl sent on an errand for her mother.

On 11 April 2022, loyalists of the newly appointed Chairman of the Lagos parks and garages committee, MC Oluomo, clashed with NURTW members in Fagba (Ifo, Lagos) when the loyalists attempted to take control of motor parks from NURTW members. The clash escalated to Ogba (Ifako LGA) and Pen Cinema (coded separately); many persons were wounded.
On 23 May 2020, rival Amankwo Communal militias clashed in Afikpo North LGA (Ebonyi) and killed another resident.

On 14 September 2022, policemen clashed with a Katsina militia who were not fewer than 30 that attempted to rob civilians and blocked the Sabuwa-Mararabar Yakawada road (Sabuwa, Katsina). One of the assailants was killed, one rifle and four motorcycles were recovered from the scene by policemen.
On 24 December 2021, two suspected rival cult groups clashed in Igbokoda (Ilaje, Ondo). The clash was related to disputes over oil rich areas by the cult groups. Five persons were killed.
On 6 May 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians and abducted eighteen others at Ungwan Dantata in Kallah ward (Kachia, Kaduna). The assailants invaded the area on foot.
On 31 March 2021, an armed group attacked and killed three policemen in Essien Udim LGA (Akwa Ibom), coded to Ikot Ebak. Four policemen were missing.
On 3 April 2020 (or around), residents of Oto-Awori (Ojo LGA, Lagos) engaged in a street-fight over the delivery of coronavirus relief materials. Several people were injured.

On 17 February 2023, some demonstrators who are residents of Ore set bonfires on both sides of the expressway while demonstrating on Ore-Benin expressway (Odigbo, Ondo) over the scarcity of new naira notes.

Property destruction: On 25 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to have been sponsored by the APC destroyed ballot boxes and chased away voters at Akerele in Oworonsoki (Kosofe, Lagos).

On 6 July 2021, about 270 suspected members of a militia attacked the village of Tsauwa, Batsari LGA (Katsina) [coded Batsari]. Between 19 and 21 residents were killed and many houses were set on fire.

On 3 December 2022, hundreds of Boko Haram [JAS] fighters led by Ali Ngulde attacked and clashed with ISWAP fighters in the camp of Yuwe coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). At least 12 ISWAP fighters were killed and their weapons were seized. Other sources report that the JAS fighters ambushed ISWAP after a failed negotiation that was initiated by JAS.
On 7 August 2024, a Plateau militia shot and killed a woman and injured her daughter in Kikyau village in Mangu LGA, coded to Mangu (Plateau). The daughter managed to escape with gunshot wounds.
Looting: On 30 April 2022, ISWAP militants set up an illegal vehicle checkpoint and robbed civilians in the Dikwa area (Dikwa, Borno). There were two checkpoints in the area.
On 25 October 2023, the Ogwuaniocha community residents protested in Ogwuaniocha, coded to Awka (Awka South, Anambra), over the clash that resulted in ten fatalities between two youth groups.

On 21 September 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with Benue Communal militia members trying to attack Ortese and Ukoholin, coded to Ndzorov (Guma, Benue). An unspecified number of the militiamen were killed and their bodies were taken away by the other militiamen. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 3 February 2021, residents attempted to lynch two suspected robbers at Sagamu Road in Sabo Community (Ikorodu LGA, Lagos). Police forces rescued the victims.
On 19 April 2021, Ezzilo militiamen clashed with Iyionu militiamen at Ishielu LGA (Ebonyi) [coded to Ezillo] over a lingering boundary dispute. Two reported fatalities.

On 5 May 2024, a Kaduna militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers and police forces who responded to a distress call in Ambe (Sanga, Kaduna). 6 civilians were killed and 8 others were injured before the troops arrived, one of the assailants was arrested while the others fled with injuries.

On 19 July 2024, Mafa defense militia ambushed and clashed with ISWAP fighters attempting to extort levies from a Fulani settlement around Mafa (Tarmua, Yobe). Nine people, including two defense militia members and seven ISWAP fighters, were killed.

On 5 June 2020, traders resisted the NSCDC officers carrying out the demolition of a black market at Ekpri Ikang (Akpabuyo LGA, Cross River). NSCDC responded with gun fire and killed 2 youths. A jeep of NSCDC was burnt.

On 17 March 2024, residents who were affected by the demolition that took place in Ona Ara LGA and Oluyole LGA protested and demanded for the intervention of the state governor. Location coded to Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo).

On 3 February 2024, Boko Haram militants (JAS faction) planted an IED which detonated after the vehicle of the commander of sector 2 of the joint task force of Operation Hadain Kai ran over it at Kukareta (Damaturu, Yobe). One soldier was wounded in the leg, the vehicle was damaged and the commander was unharmed.
On 14 July 2020, Nigerian Armed Forces clashed with Zamfara Communal Militias at Komani Hills in Rukudawa area of Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). 6 militiamen were killed and equipment seized.

On 24 October 2021, security forces engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Megezoji (Dan-Musa, Katsina), coded as Dan Musa. Domestic animals were recovered from the militia's camp, casualties unknown.
Around 1 January 2021 (as reported), Nigerian Airforce conducted air strikes against a Kaduna communal militia in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna), killing several militiamen. Several fatalities coded as 3.

On 27 February 2022, Niger militiamen attacked civilians at Ndaruka (Lavun, Niger), Ndagbegi, Ebbo, Tshogi, Ndakogitu and Gogata [coded separately]. Over 5000 persons were displaced. Casualties unknown.

On 3 September 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists hacked a farmer to death and injured two others in the Ruwaza community (Abaji, FCT). The farmer challenged the pastoralists for grazing their cows on the farm, and the altercation that followed led to his death.

On 10 May 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in conjunction with troops of sector 4, MNJTF engaged ISWAP militants who attempted to them in an armed clash at Arege (Abadan, Borno). Several militants were killed, together with aerial support from the air task force, a VBIED was destroyed, other sources report that about 10 militants were killed and two of their vehicles were destroyed. ISWAP claimed that the attack was a successful detonation of a VBIED that killed, wounded soldiers, damaged and destroyed several vehicles.

On 11 April 2023, students of Ekiti state university blocked the school's main gate while protesting in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti) over claims that their school fees and other charges were increased.

On 28 August 2021, two sets of protesters in support of Secondus and Wike protested at the secretariat of the PDP at Wuse, (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Secondus supporters called for the continuation of his tenure as party chairman, Wike supporters protested in solidarity to him.
On 23 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed three farmers on their farms at Odugbo (Apa, Benue). One person sustained serious injuries and was rushed to the hospital.

On 17 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted 86 - 87 civilians during an attack on Kajuru Station (Kajuru, Kaduna). The militia also broke into shops and stole food items, there are no reports on ransom demands. Other sources report that the incident happened at Tantatu and Aguba villages in Kufana district.

On 27 April 2021, a mob of unknown persons attacked journalist at Rumuagholu community located along the Airport Road in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). There were no fatalities. The attackers stole and destroyed their personal and professional items including HDV cameras and recorders. The victims were from various media houses who were invited for a press briefing by the king and chiefs of Rumuagholu.
On 8 July 2024, a Zamfara militia clashed with the Kaya defense militia in Kaya village (Maradun, Zamfara). No further details.

On 12 October 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked 3 members of a local self defense militia who were drinking at a pub in Igbo-Ukwu community (Aguata, Anambra) and killed them. Some sources report that the assailants were members of a kidnap syndicate who killed the victims because they curtailed their activities, other sources report that the assailants were members of a separatist group that considered the victims to be Ebube Agu operatives and their rivals.

On 4 July 2020, troops of Operation DELTA SAFE conducted a raid on pirates/militants' camp at Tukugbene Ayama, Southern Ijaw LGA (Bayelsa), coded to Oporoma. 5 people were killed and an unspecified number were injured. 5 AK47 rifles were recovered.

Around 8 July 2020 (as reported), suspected land grabbers attacked civilians at the property of the One Love Family sect along the Lagos-Ibadan expressway (location coded as Ibadan, Ibadan North West LGA, Oyo) and injured 4 members of the sect.

On 6 August 2023, a Katsina militia engaged troops of sector 2 of Operation Hadarin Daji who were on a routine patrol in an armed clash along Jibia-Magama-Maidabaru road (Jibia, Katsina). Three members of the militia were killed and two soldiers were wounded.

On 15 March 2021, women and youth residents with leaders and members of PDP staged a protest along the Akiewhe-Owhe-Ughelli-Asaba Road (Oshimili South LGA, Delta) over the state governor's decision to replace the late majority leader of the state House of Assembly.
